snippet.title: Fake Guru Tai Lopez Sued For Running $112 MILLION PONZI SCHEME
snippet.description:
Fake guru Tai Lopez has been formally accused by the SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) — along with several associates — of running a massive $112 million Ponzi scheme and investor fraud operation. This case centers on Retail Ecommerce Ventures (REV), the company where Lopez pitched investors on buying distressed and bankrupt brick‑and‑mortar brands (like Pier 1, RadioShack and other iconic stores) with the promise of transforming them into profitable online‑only businesses.

According to the SEC’s complaint, Lopez allegedly misused investor funds, paying old investors with money from new investors while failing to generate real profits — a classic Ponzi scheme. The lawsuit also accuses Lopez of funding his lavish lifestyle with investor money rather than delivering the “huge returns” he promised.

If the allegations are upheld, this case could be referred to the Department of Justice, where Tai Lopez could face up to 20 years in prison if found guilty.

Follow @Rookcommentary for more!

snippet.title: Tai Lopez The Original FAKE GURU | 10+ Years of Grifting
snippet.description:
Tai Lopez is one of the original fake gurus—the man who helped pioneer the internet coaching industry we see everywhere in 2025. For over a decade, he’s released program after program, chasing every trending niche in hopes of cashing in: self-help, dating, SMMA, crypto, real estate… you name it.

In this video, I trace his story from the early 2000s—starting with a nightclub in North Carolina—to his now-scrubbed dating company (Elite Global Dating LLC), the rise of his infamous 67 Steps program, and everything that followed. Along the way, I break down the repeating patterns: recycled funnels, exaggerated claims, and a carefully crafted persona built on borrowed authority.

snippet.title: The Rise and Fall of Instagram’s Biggest SCAMMER (Stole Millions)
snippet.description:
Ramon Abbas, better known as Hushpuppi, was one of the internet’s most infamous Instagram scammers and online fraudsters. Growing up in Nigeria, he started with small romance scams before moving on to massive wire fraud and money laundering schemes — climaxing in an attempt to defraud a Premier League team for over $100 million.

What made Hushpuppi different was his obsession with flexing. His luxury lifestyle on Instagram — private jets, designer clothes, and supercars — wasn’t to sell a course or a coaching program like today’s fake gurus and alpha males. He flaunted it simply to show off. But it was this need for attention that ultimately ruined him.

In 2020, Hushpuppi was arrested in Dubai, extradited to the United States, and convicted on federal fraud charges. He was sentenced to 11 years in prison, bringing down one of the flashiest scammers the world has ever seen.

👉 Would you trade 11 years in prison for $20 million? Let me know your thoughts in the comments.

Thank you for the support! Follow @Rookcommentary for more!
